# [CS041] gRPC Server Without Resource Limits (grpc-server-missing-limits)

A gRPC server sets neither stream limits nor an interceptor, or allows very large messages.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | MEDIUM |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-400](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html) |
| **OWASP** | A06:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Without MaxConcurrentStreams or an interceptor enforcing limits, one client can open unlimited streams; a MaxRecvMsgSize above 64 MiB lets a single message exhaust memory. Options built in another function are not judged.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
srv := grpc.NewServer(grpc.MaxRecvMsgSize(1 << 30))
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
srv := grpc.NewServer(
	grpc.MaxConcurrentStreams(100),
	grpc.MaxRecvMsgSize(4<<20),
	grpc.ChainUnaryInterceptor(rateLimit, auth),
)
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [grpc-server-missing-limits]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    grpc-server-missing-limits: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore grpc-server-missing-limits -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** grpc-server-missing-limits
```
